criterion: A language qualifies when semantic relationships commonly expressed with English 'for' require or commonly use more than one pedagogically distinct word, case marker, particle, postposition, preposition, or construction. This is broader than an exact Spanish-style two-preposition split.
discovery_method: Candidate discovery uses sense-separated English 'for' translation tables plus language-specific grammar/dictionary checks. Discovery is not human linguistic approval.
notes: confirmed_multi means discovery evidence is sufficient to include the language in the lesson-family research graph; it does not mean its detailed rules are reviewed or lesson-ready.
research_required languages remain explicit rows in scope. Agents should resolve them rather than silently omitting them.

2026-09-22 candidate research resolved bg, et, is and tr at discovery level: Bulgarian separates beneficiary/basic za, causal zaradi/poradi and purpose-clause za da; Estonian uses distinct eest/jaoks and cause-oriented postpositions such as parast/tottu; Icelandic contrasts benefactive fyrir with duration i + accusative; Turkish contrasts icin purpose/benefit with duration morphology such as -DIr. These are research-graph inclusions, not reviewed lesson rules.

2026-09-22 candidate research also resolved az, ka, mk and uz at discovery level: Azerbaijani distinguishes ucun from gora and other cause expressions; Georgian has genitive -tvis 'for' versus gamo 'because of'; Macedonian uses za alongside distinct causal poradi/zaradi and da-based purpose constructions; Uzbek uses uchun for purpose/benefit while duration may be bare or expressed with davomida. These remain candidate research facts, not lesson-ready rules.
The audit must be regenerated from the canonical learnerCapable registry whenever that registry changes.
